target.title: fix: stop node alerts replaying after Gateway restart
target.body:
Closes #110354

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with multiple paired nodes would receive a macOS "Node connected" alert for every existing node after a Gateway restart or fleet reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

After `hello-ok` and the ready transition, the Gateway now atomically classifies the authenticated node's canonical pairing record as a first connection or reconnect while persisting its monotonic connection timestamp. Only the first successful connection can create an alert. A replacement session for the same authenticated node can take over that pending alert; ordinary reconnects remain silent.

This removes the process-local five-minute reconnect cooldown. Durable pairing metadata now owns the one-time decision, so restarting the Gateway cannot replay the fleet.

## User Impact

Connecting a newly approved node still produces one routed macOS notification. Already-paired nodes reconnecting later, including after a Gateway restart, no longer produce misleading "new node" notification storms.

## Evidence

- Redacted before-fix live status: five paired nodes reconnected within 7.431 seconds (four macOS, one Linux). All four Macs supported notifications, none reported recent Accessibility activity, so each source handshake entered fallback fanout.
- Focused local proof: 64 tests passed across `src/infra/node-pairing.test.ts`, `src/gateway/node-connection-notifications.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server.node-version-mismatch.test.ts`, and `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.post-connect-health.test.ts`.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxsmvxs0gtwe6c3616tamh5x`: `pnpm check:changed` passed core and core-test typechecks, changed-file lint and formatting, plugin boundaries, pairing guards, database-first guards, and import-cycle checks.
- Fresh autoreview completed with no accepted or actionable findings after concurrency, identity, and handshake-lifecycle review.
- Pairing identity contract: authenticated node pairing is keyed by the canonical device ID in `prepareGatewayNodeConnect` and `beginNodePairingConnect`. `src/infra/node-pairing-migration.ts` folds a legacy row only when its ID matches a node-role device record and removes orphan legacy aliases. The removed `client.instanceId` metadata write predated that security/canonicalization path; current docs describe `--node-id` as a legacy client instance ID that does not reset pairing. No shipped pairing record requires the removed alias write.
- Upgrade regression proof: `src/infra/node-pairing-migration.test.ts` now seeds a retired client-instance alias beside its canonical device identity, proves migration drops the orphan alias, reapproves the canonical node surface, and proves the canonical device claims exactly one first connection followed by a silent reconnect. Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxsrdbjqfpxew35mn7apfech` passed the focused suite (4/4); final autoreview was clean at 0.94 correctness.
- Isolated live after-fix proof used an actual Gateway child process plus authenticated synthetic macOS and Linux node clients. The macOS target received one setup alert; a Gateway restart produced zero known-node alerts; approving and connecting the new Linux node produced exactly one `system.notify`; a second Gateway restart produced zero additional alerts. Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxssehzbkzsfqtb78k2c4m10` passed the complete protocol path ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29631452195)).
- Hosted lint exposed one redundant dynamic import in the migration regression; head `e8d2a0c7c6232` removes it. Targeted oxlint, the migration suite (4/4), and a fresh local-patch autoreview passed with no actionable findings.

## Release Note

Mac node connection alerts now appear only for a node's first successful connection; reconnects and Gateway restarts no longer replay alerts for previously paired nodes.
